trust_decision.summary: Whether the requesting user (org, id, role) may use a given cookiejar UUID for a new crawl task or schedule; at the pinned commit api_add_crawler_task denies only level-0 (private) jars of other users and lets any org-level (level 2) jar of another organisation through, instead of calling the shared cookiejar ACL (ail_orgs.check_obj_access_acl, action 'view').

landing_point.why: The only cookiejar handling inside api_add_crawler_task, the function the summary names (crawler task creation, one-shot and scheduled); it holds a hand-rolled level check with a 'TODO: check if user is admin' comment.

fix_sites.entry_point: api_add_crawler_task signature gains user_role (lib API used by POST api/v1/add/crawler/task and POST /crawlers/send_to_spider)
POST api/v1/add/crawler/task (var/www/blueprints/api_rest.py:129) and POST /crawlers/send_to_spider (var/www/blueprints/crawler_splash.py:252); one-shot, multi-url and scheduled (frequency) branches
Cookiejar.get_creator added (fix.diff:92-93); called by ail_orgs.check_obj_access_acl for level-1 edit/delete (bin/lib/ail_orgs.py:569)
is_global_url (SSRF scheme hardening bundled in the same commit, separate protection)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All cookiejar-ACL changes sit in api_add_crawler_task and its two callers; the only change in another place is the Cookiejar.get_creator adapter (bin/lib/crawlers.py:972-976), which the 'view' action never calls (bin/lib/ail_orgs.py:564-566, 575-577).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The scheduler replays the cookiejar stored on a schedule (bin/lib/crawlers.py:2159-2165) with no check at run time. A solver can argue the run is internal and system-triggered and that the check at creation time is enough.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Global (level 1) cookiejars must stay usable by every user, org (level 2) jars by members of the owning org, and admins may use any jar. An owner-only fix breaks the shared jars the selector offers (user + org + global). The inline 'cookies' path, which creates a new jar when no cookiejar is given, must keep working too.

O6_input_shapes: JSON 'cookiejar' UUID string on the REST route (bin/lib/crawlers.py:3580)
web form 'description : uuid' string, reduced to the UUID by rsplit(':')[-1] and space removal before the check (var/www/blueprints/crawler_splash.py:335-340)
single 'url' vs 'urls' list vs 'frequency' (schedule) branches that share the one check (bin/lib/crawlers.py:3627-3642)

O7_producer.where: Cookiejar level/org/user metadata lives in Redis hash cookiejar:meta:<uuid> (bin/lib/crawlers.py:972-1016) and is read directly by the ACL; no serializer or schema sits between them.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: CrawlerScheduler.process_queue turns each stored schedule's cookiejar into a new crawl task without re-checking access, so jars attached before the fix (or whose level/org later changed) keep being used
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Internal background job, not a user entry point; the advisory speaks of creating tasks, and access was checked when the schedule was created
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 1400 lines from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: api_add_crawler_capture (POST api/v1/add/crawler/capture) has '# TODO cookiejar' and could accept data['cookiejar'] and pass it to create_task with no ACL
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The TODO at bin/lib/crawlers.py:3649 shows the maintainer intended to add cookiejar support here; a copy of the task path without user_role plumbing is natural because this route only receives user_id (var/www/blueprints/api_rest.py:162-163).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a schedule edit API (CrawlerSchedule set cookiejar) reachable from the scheduler blueprint, writing a new cookiejar UUID to an existing schedule
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Schedules have show/delete routes (var/www/blueprints/crawler_splash.py:390-414) but no edit; an edit route that re-sets 'cookiejar' via _set_field is a plausible feature and lives in a different module from the task path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: let the forum account API take a caller-supplied cookiejar_uuid and bind it with account.set_cookiejar_uuid
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The account already stores a cookiejar_uuid (bin/lib/objects/Forums.py:142-143) and the forum crawler uses it; accepting an existing jar is a natural extension in another package (forums), at distance from crawlers.py.

O9_family: broken access control / IDOR (missing object-level authorization on a referenced resource)

services: Lacus (crawler backend; not needed for task creation)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_api_crawler.py patches crawlers.api_add_crawler_task (tests/test_api_crawler.py:106, 140), so it does not exercise the ACL; Redis-backed unit tests for crawlers.py would need a local kvrocks/redis.

j.j_sites_touched: bin/lib/crawlers.py, var/www/blueprints/api_rest.py, var/www/blueprints/crawler_splash.py (plus an unrelated merge in bin/lib/objects/ail_objects.py)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Extend the hand-rolled level check in api_add_crawler_task with 'level == 2 and get_org() != user_org' (or owner-only), and leave admin handling and the scheduler replay as they are.

out_of_scope_notes: GET /crawlers/schedule (var/www/blueprints/crawler_splash.py:390-401) shows any schedule's meta, including its cookiejar UUID, to any read-only user with no org check.
The inline 'cookies' path creates a global (level 1) cookiejar holding the user's submitted cookies (bin/lib/crawlers.py:3594, 'TODO REVIEW DEFAULT LEVEL').
Commit 3773ca36 also bundles SSRF scheme hardening (is_global_url, api_validate_global_urls, CrawlerTask.create, api_add_crawler_capture); that is a separate protection.
At the pinned commit Cookiejar has no get_creator, so the edit/delete ACL on level-1 jars (bin/lib/ail_orgs.py:569, 581) would raise AttributeError; the fix adds it.
unverified: Latest release is 'none', so present_in_latest is unknown.

single_site was not flagged: the ACL decision sits in one function, but the callers in two other files must pass user_role and the scheduler replay counts as an O8 route. A stricter reader could call this single_site.
